We are given the equation
$$0.2(2x-1) - 0.5(3x-1) = 0.4$$
We want to find the value of $x$. First, we distribute the constants to the terms inside the parentheses:
$$0.2(2x) - 0.2(1) - 0.5(3x) - 0.5(-1) = 0.4$$
$$0.4x - 0.2 - 1.5x + 0.5 = 0.4$$
Combine the terms with $x$:
$$0.4x - 1.5x - 0.2 + 0.5 = 0.4$$
$$(0.4 - 1.5)x + (0.5 - 0.2) = 0.4$$
$$-1.1x + 0.3 = 0.4$$
Now, subtract $0.3$ from both sides of the equation:
$$-1.1x = 0.4 - 0.3$$
$$-1.1x = 0.1$$
Divide both sides by $-1.1$:
$$x = \frac{0.1}{-1.1}$$
To get rid of the decimals, multiply the numerator and denominator by 10:
$$x = \frac{0.1 \times 10}{-1.1 \times 10}$$
$$x = \frac{1}{-11}$$
$$x = -\frac{1}{11}$$

Now, we check our answer:
$$0.2(2(-\frac{1}{11})-1) - 0.5(3(-\frac{1}{11})-1)$$
$$0.2(-\frac{2}{11}-1) - 0.5(-\frac{3}{11}-1)$$
$$0.2(-\frac{2}{11}-\frac{11}{11}) - 0.5(-\frac{3}{11}-\frac{11}{11})$$
$$0.2(-\frac{13}{11}) - 0.5(-\frac{14}{11})$$
$$-\frac{0.2(13)}{11} + \frac{0.5(14)}{11}$$
$$-\frac{2.6}{11} + \frac{7}{11}$$
$$\frac{-2.6+7}{11}$$
$$\frac{4.4}{11} = \frac{44}{110} = \frac{2}{5} = 0.4$$
So our answer is correct.

Final Answer: The final answer is $\boxed{-1/11}$
